current_p1_ru: Дорога, Затонувший мир, Притча о сеятеле, Голодные игры. Тебе ближе антиутопии после конца. Не «общество, которое стало плохим»; а общество, которое уже разрушено.
current_p1_en:
The Road, The Drowned World, Parable of the Sower, The Hunger Games. The dystopias closest to you are set after the end. Not a society turning bad, but one already destroyed.
Why this lands: you have a survival instinct. These books are about what remains when everything's gone, and that's where your interest lies.
Other people sometimes worry: "are you preparing for the end of the world?". Not preparing — studying. Different things.
What's worth knowing: post-apocalyptic books rarely offer hope. Read only those and you develop a black view of the future. Balance with books about possible better worlds.

current_p1_ru: Машина останавливается, Механическое пианино, Этот идеальный день, Не отпускай меня. Тебя цепляют антиутопии о технологии. Не «государство»; а технологический прогресс как угроза.
current_p1_en:
The Machine Stops, Player Piano, This Perfect Day, Never Let Me Go. The dystopias that grab you are about technology. Not the state itself, but technological progress as a threat.
The logic is simple: you have a critical view of progress. Most see only benefit in tech; you understand every innovation has a dark side.
Other people sometimes call you a "luddite". Not a luddite. Just understand technology isn't neutral.
What's worth knowing: tech dystopias often turn out to be predictions. The Machine Stops (1909) is today's society in caricature. Learn to read them as a map of the future, not as fiction.

current_p1_ru: Железная пята, Голодные игры, Притча о сеятеле, Рассказ служанки. Тебя цепляют антиутопии о власти небольшой группы над большинством. Не «один диктатор»; а классовая система, которая воспроизводит себя.
current_p1_en:
The Iron Heel, The Hunger Games, Parable of the Sower, The Handmaid's Tale. What grabs you are dystopias about a small group holding power over the majority. Not one dictator, but a class system that reproduces itself.
This works because you have a social instinct. These books are about the persistence of inequality, and that's close to reality.
Other people sometimes accuse: "you're a leftist". Not a leftist — a realist.
What's worth knowing: books about class struggle often radicalize. Learn to separate the literary from the political. Good dystopia is both warning and art, not propaganda.

current_p1_ru: Затонувший мир, Притча о сеятеле, Дорога, Машина останавливается. Тебе важна экологическая антиутопия. Не «социальная»; а как природа становится врагом или жертвой.
current_p1_en:
The Drowned World, Parable of the Sower, The Road, The Machine Stops. Ecological dystopia matters to you. Not only social collapse, but the moment nature becomes enemy, victim, or both.
Why it works: you have a deep instinct for nature. Most people don't yet believe in the climate crisis; you do.
Other people sometimes say: "you're an alarmist". Alarmist. And literature shows the alarm is justified.
What's worth knowing: climate dystopias are increasingly relevant. Read them in the context of current events. Each year a new heat record makes Ballard's Drowned World (1962) closer to us.

current_p1_ru: Discord, Twitch, Reddit, YouTube — твоя среда. Это не «соцсети для коммуникации», это место, где ты живёшь параллельную социальную жизнь — со стримерами, клано-чатами, мемами своей субкультуры.
current_p1_en:
Discord, Twitch, Reddit, YouTube — that's your environment. These aren't just social networks for communication; they're where you live a parallel social life, with streamers, clan chats, and the memes of your subculture.
It works because you have a deep world that others are just tourists in. You have lore, history, favorite figures, specific jokes. It's a full second life, and it's just as real to you as the regular one.
People sometimes devalue it: "those aren't real relationships". And you know — they're real. Just living in a different context. You can be friends with someone 5000 km away, and that doesn't make the friendship less real.
What's worth knowing: online communities are strong, but give one specific form of closeness. Without offline contacts it becomes isolation over time. Learn to mix: online friends + at least 2-3 people in the physical world you see in person. Otherwise after 5 years, life is heavily skewed into one register.

items_in_category: Voice notes longer than a minute
current_p1_ru: Голосовые длиннее минуты, кружочки видео, сухие «ок». Ты предпочитаешь не печатать. Голос быстрее, лицо живее, текст — это для слабых.
current_p1_en:
Voice messages longer than a minute, video circles, dry "ok". You prefer not to type. Voice is faster, the face is livelier, text feels too flat.
The logic is simple: speech is your strong side. Text limits you; in voice, you're yourself.
People sometimes complain: "another five-minute voice message!" Another one, yes. If reading is inconvenient, listen.
What's worth knowing: voice messages cost the recipient time. You gave yourself speed; you gave them five minutes of listening and no way to skim. Learn when voice is fine and when text is better, especially for requests or important facts. Voice is a gift to you. Text is a gift to them.

items_in_category: Voice notes longer than a minute
current_p1_ru: Простыни текста, идеальная пунктуация, переписываешь по 5 раз, эмодзи и восклицания. Ты делаешь сообщения как маленькие документы.
current_p1_en:
Walls of text, perfect punctuation, you rewrite five times, emojis and exclamations. You make messages like little documents.
Why it works: you have respect for form. Most write "however it comes out"; you believe even in chat it's worth writing properly.
People sometimes are surprised: "you don't have to use commas in chat". Don't have to — but I prefer it. And the recipient too, I hope.
What's worth knowing: perfectionism in chats eats time. If you rewrite a message five times, that's no longer a chat, it's a letter. Learn to let go. Not every message has to be perfect. Some thoughts are best delivered raw — the polish steals the moment.

items_in_category: Voice notes longer than a minute
current_p1_ru: Стикеры вместо слов, мемы вместо ответа, кружочки, ссылка без контекста. У тебя текст — последний инструмент. Сначала картинка, мем, видео, ссылка.
current_p1_en:
Stickers instead of words, memes instead of replies, video circles, links without context. For you, text is the last tool. First a picture, meme, video, link.
The reason it works: you have visual thinking. You're faster at "finding the right meme" than formulating in words.
People sometimes don't accept it: "a sticker isn't an answer". It's an answer. Just in another language.
What's worth knowing: visual communication works with those who understand it. With your mom, a sticker instead of "how are you" isn't "modern", it's "you're not answering". Learn to adapt to the recipient. Your favorite language isn't universal; with some people, words are still the way through.

items_in_category: Voice notes longer than a minute
current_p1_ru: Эмодзи и восклицания, «ахах» без эмоций, идеальная пунктуация, переписываешь по 5 раз. У тебя сообщения насыщены эмоциональными маркерами, даже когда внутри ничего особо.
current_p1_en:
Emojis and exclamations, "haha" without emotion, perfect punctuation, you rewrite five times. Your messages are saturated with emotional markers, even when there's nothing particular inside.
It works because you understand: text doesn't carry intonation. Without an emoji, the phrase "ok" reads as offense; with an emoji, as light agreement.
People sometimes say: "why 100 exclamation marks?". So it's clear I'm not offended, but really agreeing.
What's worth knowing: "haha" without emotion turns into background. If you write it automatically, the recipient stops taking your "haha" seriously. Learn to use emotional markers more rarely but more precisely. Saved for the moments that need them, they keep their meaning.

items_in_category: Voice notes longer than a minute
current_p1_ru: Читаешь, но не отвечаешь, отвечаешь через сутки, «ща» и пропадаешь, ссылка без слов. Ты непредсказуем(-а) в переписке. Можешь быть онлайн, но не реагировать.
current_p1_en:
You read but don't reply, answer a day later, "brb" and disappear, link without words. You're unpredictable in messaging. You can be online but not react.
Why this lands: you have your own tempo. You don't believe you have to answer immediately; that's your freedom.
People sometimes get offended: "you saw the message". I saw it. Not in the mood right now.
What's worth knowing: silence after reading = worse than no reply. If the other person sees you "read but stayed silent", it's interpreted as "they don't want to talk". Learn to at least reply briefly: "saw it, will answer later". A two-second message saves a relationship from a day of silent doubt.

items_in_category: Voice notes longer than a minute
current_p1_ru: Отвечаешь моментально, голосовые, спам коротких сообщений, кружочки. Ты в мессенджере живёшь. Ответ через 30 секунд — норма; через 5 минут — уже задержка.
current_p1_en:
You answer instantly, voice messages, spam of short messages, video circles. You live in the messenger. Reply in 30 seconds — normal; in 5 minutes — already a delay.
The logic is simple: your nervous system is tuned to fast communication. You're bored waiting; you need the dynamic of a conversation.
People sometimes are surprised: "don't you work?". I work. Just answer in parallel.
What's worth knowing: instant reply eats focus. If you're in chat every minute, you're not really working. Learn to turn off notifications at least an hour a day. The best work happens in silence. Your speed is a strength; protecting it from itself is the next level.

current_p1_ru: Кринж, душнила, криповый — твой словарный запас. Ты остро видишь, когда что-то фальшиво, и не молчишь об этом. Твой стиль — это критика через мемы: точная, режущая, иногда жестокая.
current_p1_en:
Cringe, dushnila (the dry, tedious one), creepy — your vocabulary. You sharply see when something is fake, and don't stay silent about it. Your style is criticism through memes: precise, cutting, sometimes cruel.
This works because you don't buy the shiny. You see a cheap move in a film — you'll mark it as cringe. You see a tedious blogger — you'll call them dushnila. You can't be fooled, and so your circle of communication respects this.
People sometimes fear you a bit: "it's scary to joke around you, you'll immediately tear it apart". You won't tear it apart — you'll mark it. That's different. But they don't fully believe it.
What's worth knowing: criticism is a great skill, but also dangerous. If everything is always "cringe" or "dushnila" for you — you're no longer a critic, you're background of denial. Over time this destroys the ability to feel joy. Learn to tell real failures from just "not mine". Not every "not mine" deserves your strike.

current_p1_ru: Сигма, скуф, альтушка, дед-инсайд — ты узнаёшь себя в этих ярлыках. Не серьёзно, а с самоиронией. «Ну да, я как раз скуф» — и ты этим даже доволен. Возможность поставить на себя ярлык даёт тебе ощущение принадлежности.
current_p1_en:
Sigma, skuf (the slipping middle-aged guy), altushka (the alt girl), dead inside — you recognize yourself in these labels. Not seriously — with self-irony. "Yeah, I'm exactly a skuf" — and you're even glad. The chance to put a label on yourself gives you a feeling of belonging.
This works because memes have become a tool of self-definition. Earlier people defined themselves through Jung's questions, now — through TikTok archetypes. This isn't superficial; it's just a new language for an old thing.
People sometimes tease you: "you're really a typical sigma". You smile. They don't understand that for you, "being a typical sigma" is neither an insult nor a compliment, just stating belonging to a tribe.
What's worth knowing: labels are a convenient language, but they simplify. If you describe yourself only through them, you lose the nuances of your personality. The same person can be sigma, skuf, and emo at once — depending on mood. Don't cling to a label as identity. It's a hat, not a head.

current_p1_ru: Бумер, зумер, скуф, альтушка — ты используешь эти термины как карту мира. Ты понимаешь, к какому поколению относишься, и видишь, как другие поколения отличаются. И иронизируешь по обе стороны границы.
current_p1_en:
Boomer, zoomer, skuf, altushka — you use these terms as a map of the world. You understand which generation you belong to, and you see how other generations differ. And you ironize on both sides of the border.
This works because you see generations as different cultures. They have different language, different values, different ideas of what's proper. And not "right-wrong", but "different". This interests you.
People sometimes accuse you of ageism: "you discriminate against boomers". And you don't discriminate — you study them anthropologically. Through memes. That's a real tool.
What's worth knowing: generational division is convenient but crude. Within a generation there are also different people, and sometimes a zoomer with a boomer is closer to each other than with their "peers". Learn to see a person not as a representative of a generation, but as a person. Otherwise you're a captive of labels and miss interesting people on the other side.

current_p1_ru: Чики-брики, камон бро, чушпан, база — у тебя коллекция фольклора. Эти слова не из учебников; они из подвалов интернета, из субкультур, из неожиданных источников. И ты умеешь к ним относиться — не свысока, а как к части культурного наследия.
current_p1_en:
Chiki-briki, c'mon bro, chushpan, baza — you have a folklore collection. These words aren't from textbooks; they're from internet basements, from subcultures, from unexpected sources. And you know how to relate to them — not from above, but as part of cultural heritage.
This works because for you, internet folklore is the folk art of the 21st century. Earlier people passed each other ditties, now — memes and phrases. It's the same culture, just in a new wrapper.
People sometimes don't get it how you remember all these words and where they came from. You don't remember — you live among them. It's not "collecting", it's "ordinary language".
What's worth knowing: folklore is a great environment, but it ages quickly. What was the base two years ago — now is cringe. Learn to feel when your vocabulary is fresh and when — already grandpa-tier (by internet standards). Refreshing the dictionary is part of life in a living culture.

current_p1_ru: Криповый, дед-инсайд, альтушка, кринж — твой набор слов сосредоточен в тёмной палитре. Ты умеешь видеть жуткое в обычном и обычное в жутком. Твой юмор — на стыке готики и мема.
current_p1_en:
Creepy, dead inside, altushka, cringe — your set of words is concentrated in a dark palette. You can see the eerie in the ordinary and the ordinary in the eerie. Your humor is at the junction of gothic and meme.
This works because you have a different sensitivity. Most want "the light, bright, kind". You choose "the strange, uncomfortable, real". And in this — most of the art that survives centuries.
People sometimes shy away: "you're kind of eerie". You smile. They got used to sterilized culture, and any roughness seems dangerous to them. And you in it — at home.
What's worth knowing: dark aesthetic is style and risk. Style — because depth and character. Risk — because it's easy to slip into when you want not art, but just a bad mood. Learn to tell: am I choosing this because it's beautiful, or because it's hard for me right now and I want to surround myself with my pain? The first — aesthetic. The second — a reason to take care of yourself.

current_p1_ru: Это другое, ну такое, база, душнила — ты используешь эти короткие выражения вместо длинных аргументов. Каждое из них содержит в себе целый смысловой блок, и нативные понимают тебя без расшифровки.
current_p1_en:
"That's different", "meh", "the base", "dushnila" — you use these short expressions instead of long arguments. Each contains a whole semantic block, and natives understand you without decoding.
This works because you've mastered high language density. "That's different" isn't three words, it's a whole rhetorical position that in academic style would require a paragraph. You economize, and that's not laziness — it's mastery.
People sometimes don't catch up: "what does 'baza' mean?". You don't get angry; you remember that once you didn't know either. Just different subcultures — different codes.
What's worth knowing: your language works among your own and translates badly. If you try to explain something to your parents through "that's different" and *baza*, they won't hear you. Learn to switch: with the young — your code, with others — ordinary language. Flexibility of registers is respect, not selling out.

current_p1_ru: Lo-fi, bedroom pop, sad pop, indie alt — твоя ниша. Музыка тихая, неинтенсивная, идеальная для работы, для дождя, для одиночества. Ты не ищешь «зажечь» — ты ищешь «успокоить».
current_p1_en:
Lo-fi, bedroom pop, sad pop, indie alt — your niche. Music is quiet, low-intensity, perfect for work, for rain, for solitude. You don't look to "light a fire" — you look to "calm".
This works because modern life is already too loud. Notifications, calls, ads, city noise. Music for you is an island of silence, not another source of noise.
People sometimes tease you: "you only have sad music". Not sad — calm. Those are different things. Calm doesn't make you unhappy, it restores you.
What's worth knowing: quiet music is wonderful, but sometimes the body demands the loud too. If you're only in lo-fi, you lose connection with the instinct to "move". Learn to add something rhythmic and loud sometimes — even if for 30 minutes once a week. The body will be grateful.

current_p1_ru: Pyrokinesis, Кишлак, Lida, ХХОС — твоя территория. Тёмный рэп, тревожные тексты, агрессивный саунд. Ты не ищешь «лёгкого» — наоборот, тебе важно, чтобы музыка отражала то тёмное, что у тебя внутри.
current_p1_en:
Pyrokinesis, Kishlak, Lida, KhKhOS — your territory. Dark rap, anxious lyrics, aggressive sound. You're not looking for "the light" — on the contrary, it matters to you that music reflects what's dark inside you.
This works because you have unprocessed emotions, and ordinary pop can't handle them. You need artists who don't smooth over but amplify. Then your pain becomes understandable — it has a soundtrack.
People sometimes worry: "you're listening to something too dark, are you ok?". Sometimes okay, sometimes not. But music isn't the cause here — it's the mirror. And taking the mirror from you is foolish.
What's worth knowing: dark music reflects the dark, but doesn't heal. If you're in a bad state and listen only to aggressive rap, you can amplify your state, not work through it. Learn to alternate: sometimes reflection of pain, sometimes something light for contrast. Otherwise you get stuck in one emotional tone, and it's hard to leave.

current_p1_ru: ХХОС, ICEGERGERT, Kishlak — ты в центре российской фонк-сцены. Это уникальное явление: жанр, родившийся в Мемфисе, был перепрошит русскими продюсерами в нечто узнаваемо-наше. И ты слышишь эту специфику.
current_p1_en:
KhKhOS, ICEGERGERT, Kishlak — you're in the middle of the Russian phonk scene. It's a unique phenomenon: a genre born in Memphis was reflashed by Russian producers into something recognizably ours. And you hear this specificity.
This works because you have an ear for the new. You didn't wait for phonk to become a global trend — you heard it in 2020-2021 when it was still a niche. And you still distinguish who's doing the "real thing" from who's chasing hype.
People sometimes don't get it: "that's just bass and slurred words". And you hear that inside there's structure, schools, authors. It's not homogeneous noise — it's a scene with history, even if short.
What's worth knowing: the phonk scene is quickly commercializing. What was underground in 2021 now plays in TikTok clips. Learn to track which artists keep authenticity and which sold themselves to the algorithm. That's real loyalty to the genre — following its evolution, not only consuming the top.

current_p1_ru: ANNA ASTI, HammAli & Navai, Тима Белорусских, Slava Marlow — это твой саундтрек. Лиричный поп-рэп с цеплючими припевами, романтика без лишних философий, ровно то, что ты хочешь услышать в маршрутке утром.
current_p1_en:
ANNA ASTI, HammAli & Navai, Tima Belorusskikh, Slava Marlow — that's your soundtrack. Lyrical pop-rap with catchy choruses, romance without extra philosophy, exactly what you want to hear in the morning marshrutka.
This works because you understand: sometimes you need exactly simple music. Not "deep", not "conceptual", but the kind that goes in without explanations and stays with you for weeks.
People sometimes condemn: "that's pop". And you don't feel embarrassed. Pop is actually a complex genre; making a chorus that catches millions of people is a rare skill, and these artists have it.
What's worth knowing: pop hits are passing. What now grabs the whole country, in two years will be awkward to hum. That's not bad — pop has that nature. But if you have a playlist of only current hits, you have no "eternal tracks" to return to in ten years. Learn to add the durable too, not only the fashionable.

current_p1_ru: Pyrokinesis с поэзией, Тима Белорусских с историями, Скриптонит с куплетами, HammAli с романтикой. Тебе важно, чтобы за рэпом стояло слово — настоящая работа с языком, а не просто рифмы под бит.
current_p1_en:
Pyrokinesis with poetry, Tima Belorusskikh with stories, Skriptonit with verses, HammAli with romance. It matters to you that there's a word behind the rap — real work with language, not just rhymes over a beat.
This works because you have an ear for text. Most listen to rap for the sound, you — for what's said. And so from the same tracks you extract three times more meaning.
People are sometimes surprised at your ability to quote whole verses. You didn't "learn" them — you just listened attentively, and the text stuck to memory itself, because it was well-written.
What's worth knowing: focus on the word sometimes overshadows sound. If an artist writes brilliantly but sounds average, you can overrate them. Learn to hold both filters: text OR sound — that's half; text AND sound — that's the full thing. The best artists are strong in both, and worth keeping the bar.

current_p1_ru: Big Baby Tape, Скриптонит, Платина, Lida — твоя территория. Тебе нужны куплеты, которые качают, биты, которые бьют в грудь, и подача, от которой шевелится тело.
current_p1_en:
Big Baby Tape, Skriptonit, Platina, Lida — your territory. You need verses that pump, beats that hit the chest, and delivery from which the body moves.
This works because you have a physical connection with music. You don't sit and "analyze" — you move. And so artists who make pumping music matter more to you than those who make "smart" music.
People sometimes don't get it: "nothing's said in the track". And you didn't come for "said". You came for the body to respond to sound. And when it responds — that's full communication, without words.
What's worth knowing: pumping music is great fuel, but bad company in long moments. Morning before work — yes. An evening with a friend — yes. But for a quiet evening at home or for a complex emotional moment — no. Learn to tell situations apart. Then your playlist always works.

current_p1_ru: Тейлор Свифт, Ариана Гранде, Бейонсе, Джастин Бибер — артисты, которые могут всё. Их треки звучат на свадьбах, в спортзалах, в наушниках, в супермаркетах. Они — общая валюта поп-музыки, и ты с ней дружишь.
current_p1_en:
Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande, Beyoncé, Justin Bieber — artists who can do everything. Their tracks play at weddings, in gyms, in headphones, in supermarkets. They are the common currency of pop music, and you're friendly with it.
This works because you're not embarrassed by mainstream. These artists aren't in the charts by accident — they did everything to be there. And when you need "just a good song", you go to them.
People sometimes accuse you: "you have no taste, you listen to what everyone listens to". You don't argue. Sometimes "what everyone listens to" is exactly the best. Not all mainstream is deserved, but these earned it.
What's worth knowing: pop universalists are a safe choice, but safety is boring. If you only have Taylor and Ariana in your playlist, you miss a huge layer of less mass but sometimes more interesting music. Learn to spend at least 20% of time on something less obvious. That keeps your ear in fresh shape.

current_p1_ru: Olivia Rodrigo, Billie Eilish, Lana Del Rey, ранняя Тейлор — артистки, которые перевели в музыку то, что чувствуют молодые. Любовные катастрофы как конец света, разочарования как философия, тревога как вайб.
current_p1_en:
Olivia Rodrigo, Billie Eilish, Lana Del Rey, early Taylor — artists who translated into music what young people feel. Love disasters as the end of the world, disappointments as philosophy, anxiety as a vibe.
This works because in their tracks you hear your own life. Most "adult" artists sing about things that don't touch you. And these — about what you're going through now, and that makes you feel less alone.
People sometimes devalue: "that's teenage drama". Well yeah. You have it now, and music about it isn't shame, it's support. What adults call "teenage" is often the most important.
What's worth knowing: dramatic music intensifies feelings. If you're in stress, it deepens you into stress. Learn to distinguish: when you need "feel with me" (then drama helps), and when "get out of this" (then something else is needed — energy, lightness, distraction).

current_p1_ru: Kendrick Lamar с повествованием, Frank Ocean с медитацией, Tyler с продакшном, SZA с уязвимостью. Это не «рэп для качания» — это рэп для думания. И ты с ним проводишь часы, а не минуты.
current_p1_en:
Kendrick Lamar with narrative, Frank Ocean with meditation, Tyler with production, SZA with vulnerability. This isn't "rap for pumping" — it's rap for thinking. And you spend hours with it, not minutes.
This works because you hear rap as modern literature. These artists have a story, image, idea in every track. And listening to them superficially means missing three-quarters of the value.
People are sometimes surprised: "how do you find so much in one track?". You don't "find" — it's there. Most just don't listen carefully.
What's worth knowing: intellectual rap is wonderful, but requires attention. If you listen to it as background at work — you lose the meaning. Learn to separate: this music — separately, in headphones, without multitasking. Otherwise you consume it without tasting. And then you're surprised why "I think I heard it but don't remember".

current_p1_ru: Drake, Travis Scott, Post Malone, Bad Bunny — артисты, чьи треки гремят с любого телефона на улице. Это музыка для мейнстрим-вайба, она везде, и тебе с ней по пути.
current_p1_en:
Drake, Travis Scott, Post Malone, Bad Bunny — artists whose tracks rumble from any phone on the street. This is music for mainstream vibe, it's everywhere, and you're on the road with it.
This works because you have no snobbery. If a track grabs, you don't care that millions listen to it. You don't try to stand out by taste — you just listen to what you like.
People sometimes call you out: "Drake is mass, you'd find something more interesting". You shrug. Mass — because good. That's not always true, but in the case of these guys — often yes.
What's worth knowing: trap stadium dominates now, but it won't always be that way. When the wave changes, your playlist may turn out outdated. Learn to at least periodically track what's coming next. Not to change taste, but to understand the sound landscape. Then you have both the favorite and the general map.

current_p1_ru: Arctic Monkeys, The 1975, Radiohead, Coldplay — для тебя британская/альтернативная сцена остаётся главной. Гитары, тексты, концептуальные альбомы. Ты не двинулся вместе с поп-волной в трэп — ты остался в гитарной музыке, и она тебя кормит.
current_p1_en:
Arctic Monkeys, The 1975, Radiohead, Coldplay — for you the British/alternative scene remains the main one. Guitars, lyrics, conceptual albums. You didn't move with the pop wave to trap — you stayed in guitar music, and it feeds you.
This works because you have an ear for classical instruments. In a world with more and more synthesizers and autotune, you need live guitars and a real drum kit. It's a different feeling — more grounded.
People sometimes tease you: "you're stuck in 2010?". Not stuck — chosen. Those are different things. You understand a lot is happening in indie and alt now too, just not in the charts.
What's worth knowing: guitar music indeed left the mainstream, but that doesn't mean it died. It just moved to a niche. Learn to dig niches — that's where real indie lives now, more interesting than stadium Coldplay. If you stay only with old heroes, you'll miss the live scene.

current_p1_ru: Bad Bunny, Doja Cat, Post Malone в латино-стороне, иногда Ариана с её испанскими элементами. Тебя цепляет музыка, в которой есть жара, ритм, голос карнавала. Это не «спокойная музыка» — это праздник.
current_p1_en:
Bad Bunny, Doja Cat, Post Malone on the Latin side, sometimes Ariana with her Spanish elements. What grabs you is music that has heat, rhythm, the voice of carnival. This isn't "calm music" — it's a celebration.
This works because you have inner liveliness. You need a track to fire you up, not calm you. The Latin wave dominates globally now, and you're at its center.
People sometimes don't get it: "you don't speak Spanish, how do you listen?". And you don't need to speak. Music isn't about words, it's about vibe. And the Latin vibe is recognizable without translation.
What's worth knowing: an eternal celebration tires. If you only have fiery music in your playlist, you don't let the nervous system rest. Learn to alternate: Latin in the morning for energy, something calm in the evening for relaxation. Otherwise you're constantly ready to dance — and lose the ability to just rest.

current_p1_ru: Земфира, Скриптонит, ANNA ASTI, Моргенштерн — твоя русская сцена. Ты не игнорируешь местное в пользу глобального; для тебя русская музыка — равноправная часть твоего слушания.
current_p1_en:
Zemfira, Skriptonit, ANNA ASTI, Morgenshtern — your Russian scene. You don't ignore the local in favor of the global; for you Russian music is an equal part of your listening.
This works because you understand: the language of your life is Russian, and emotions in it land deeper. An English track is interesting. A Russian one is about you.
People are sometimes surprised: "nothing interesting is being made in Russia". You smile. They just don't listen. Skriptonit did more for Russian rap than most Western rappers did for their genre. Zemfira is one of a kind.
What's worth knowing: love for the Russian scene is wonderful, but sometimes limits. These artists themselves grew on Western ones, and hearing their roots is another level of understanding. Learn to dig the Western too. Not to break from the native, but to deepen it.
